name: color-space

tools.name: convert
tools.description: Convert a color between any two of the 205 color spaces, identity included, in each space's conventional ranges (rgb 0-255, oklch L 0-1 / C 0-0.4 / H 0-360, lab L 0-100 …). The color goes in as a CSS string (`color`) or as channel values (`from` + `values`); a batch as `colors` – tuples in `from`, CSS strings, or both. Out-of-range in, unclamped out: `inRange` flags each channel against the target's conventional range (rgb below 0 means outside sRGB); null = undefined at that coordinate.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

values.description: one color in the source space, e.g. [255, 128, 0] for rgb

colors.description: a batch: one tuple (in `from`) or CSS string per color, e.g. [[255, 128, 0], '#00ff80', 'oklch(0.7 0.1 50)']

tools.name: gamut
tools.description: Which standard display gamuts hold a color — sRGB ⊂ Display P3 ⊂ Rec. 2020, each tested in its own RGB box straight from the source space, the same ladder as the color-space.io gamut pill. `smallest` is the tightest one; null = beyond Rec. 2020. Membership only: nothing is gamut-mapped.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

values.description: one color in the source space

tools.name: css
tools.description: A color as CSS Color 4 strings — rgb(), hsl(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() and color(display-p3 | a98-rgb | prophoto-rgb | srgb-linear | xyz-d65 | xyz-d50) — plus #hex inside sRGB. Converted, never gamut-mapped: a string is null where CSS would clamp it into a different color (rgb/hsl/hwb outside sRGB, lightness out of range). `gamut` is the smallest display gamut that holds the color.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

values.description: one color in the source space

notations.description: only these, by library space id (default: all)

tools.name: space
tools.description: The dossier of one color space: display name (as color-space.io shows it), description, channels + conventional ranges, defining references, provenance (year, author), illuminant/observer, encoding class, family and purpose, and its direct conversion neighbours.

name.description: the space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

tools.name: spaces
tools.description: List the 205 color spaces with display name, family, purpose, channels and one-line use. Optional filters: `query` (words matched against id, name, use line and description; best matches first), `family`, `purpose`.

tools.name: cube
tools.description: Render a conversion as a .cube LUT file (Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut, OBS, ffmpeg). The header carries the measured deviation vs the direct conversion. Pure per-channel transfers auto-emit 1D. Size ≤ 33 here (larger via the library or https://color-space.io/).

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

tools.name: shader
tools.description: The conversion as shader source – GLSL (WebGL2; WebGL1 too unless the path reads a table), WGSL (WebGPU), HLSL (DirectX, Unity, Unreal) or MSL (Metal) – with an entry function `<from>_<to>` (hyphens stripped), e.g. `vec3 rgb_oklch(vec3 c)`, plus every function on the path. Each language is differentially tested against the library and compiled on real GPUs: use it instead of writing color matrices. HLSL and MSL need the optional peer `naga-wasm` installed beside color-space.

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

tools.name: icc
tools.description: One space as an ICC v2 profile (.icc): matrix + tone curve where the space is an RGB working space (Photoshop, OS color management), a CLUT on a Lab PCS otherwise (lcms, ArgyllCMS, ImageMagick). Returned as a base64 embedded resource; `class`, `pcs` and `bytes` describe it.

name.description: the space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

grid.description: CLUT lattice points per channel, CLUT profiles only (default 33 for 3 channels; fewer = a smaller file)

tools.name: code
tools.description: The conversion as code to paste: the color-space JS call with its result and – where one exists for the space on the non-sRGB side – the colour-science (Python) equivalent verified against color-space (sRGB ↔ that space), with any named caveat. The color goes in as a CSS string or as values in `from` (default: sRGB 200, 100, 50).

from.description: source space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

to.description: target space id, e.g. 'rgb', 'oklch', 'lab', 'slog3', 'rec709' (the 'spaces' tool lists all 205)

values.description: the color in the source space

instructions: Verified color conversions between 205 spaces — call these instead of computing color math yourself, and use `shader` / `code` instead of writing conversion matrices from memory. A color goes in as a CSS string (`color`: '#ff8000', 'oklch(0.7 0.1 50)', 'rebeccapurple') or as channel values with `from`. `convert` any pair (batches too; flags values outside the target's range), `gamut` for which display gamut holds a color, `css` for CSS Color 4 strings, `space` / `spaces` for references, ranges and provenance, `cube` for a .cube LUT, `icc` for an ICC profile, `shader` for GLSL / WGSL / HLSL / MSL, `code` for the JS call and its Python equivalent.
